source_text: καὶ μόσχον παρ' ἑκάστου, καὶ προσήγαγον ἐναντίον τῆς σκηνῆς. Καὶ εἶπε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν, λέγων· Λάβε παρ' αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔσονται πρὸς τὰ ἔργα τὰ λειτουργικὰ τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου, καὶ δώσεις αὐτὰ τοῖς Λευΐταις, ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ λειτουργίαν. Καὶ λαβὼν Μωσῆς τὰς ἁμάξας καὶ τοὺς βόας, ἔδωκεν αὐτὰ τοῖς Λευΐταις. Καὶ τὰς δύο ἁμάξας καὶ τοὺς τέσσαρας βόας ἔδωκε τοῖς υἱοῖς Γεδσὼν κατὰ τὰς λειτουργίας αὐτῶν, καὶ τὰς τέσσαρας ἁμάξας καὶ τοὺς ὀκτὼ βόας ἔδωκε τοῖς υἱοῖς Μεραρὶ κατὰ τὰς λειτουργίας αὐτῶν, διὰ Ἰθάμαρ υἱοῦ Ἀαρὼν τοῦ ἱερέως· καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς Καὰθ οὐ δέδωκεν, ὅτι τὰ λειτουργήματα τοῦ ἁγίου ἔχουσιν, ἐπ' ὤμων ἀροῦσιν.» Ἀκούεις ὅπως τοῖς μὲν τὸ ἐφ' ἁμαξῶν ἄγειν τε καὶ φέρειν ἔθος, Κααθίταις δὲ μόνοις, εἰς ὤμους τὰ ἱερά; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τοῦ δὴ χάριν; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀεὶ γάρ πως ἐστὶν ἐν ἱδρῶτι μείζονι τὸ προὖχόν τε καὶ ἱερώτερον, παρέπεται δὲ αὐτῷ πάντη τε καὶ πάντως· τὸ χρῆναι πονεῖν, καὶ πρός γε δὴ τούτῳ, τὸ τληπαθεῖν, καὶ οὐκ ἐν ἴσῳ τοῖς ἄλλοις, οἵπερ ἂν εἶεν καὶ ἁγιώτεροι, καὶ ἀγχοῦ δὴ μᾶλλον οἱονείπως Θεοῦ. Ἢ οὐκ ἀληθὲς ὅ φημι; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἐν κόσμῳ μὲν οὖν τοιῷδε τὸ Λευϊτικὸν ἐλειτούργει γένος. Οἶμαι δ' ἔγωγε, μυστηρίου τύπον τὸ χρῆμα πληροῦν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς δὴ φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἐοίκασι γὰρ, οἱ μὲν δύο δῆμοι, Γεδσών τε καὶ Μεραρὶ, τοὺς ἐν νόμῳ λαοὺς ὑπαινίττεσθαι, φημὶ δὴ τὸν Ἰσραήλ· Κααθῖται δέ γε, τοὺς ἡγιασμένους ἐν Χριστῷ διὰ πίστεως. Οἷς μὲν γὰρ ἦν ἐν φροντίδι τὰ ἱστία τῆς αὐλῆς, αἱ δέῤῥεις τῆς σκηνῆς, τὰ καλύμματα καὶ οἱ στύλοι, κεφαλαί τε καὶ βάσεις, πάσσαλοί τε καὶ περιτανύσματα, καὶ ᾗ φησι τὸ Γράμμα τὸ ἱερὸν, «Πάντα τὰ περισσὰ,» δι' οὗ σημαίνεται τὸ τῆς λειτουργίας οὐκ ἀναγκαῖον. Οἱ δὲ, φέρειν ἐθαρσήθησαν τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, καὶ τὰ δι' ὧν Χριστὸς, οὐ καθ' ἕνα τρόπον, πολλαχῶς δὲ μᾶλλον καὶ πολυειδῶς σημαίνεται, ὡς κιβωτὸς, ὡς τράπεζα, καὶ ὡς χρυσῆ λυχνία, καὶ χρυσοῦν θυμιατήριον. Ἁπλοῦς γὰρ ὑπάρχων κατὰ φύσιν ὡς Θεὸς, τῇ τῆς ἐργασίας διαφορᾷ πολυτρόπως γνωρίζεται. Ἔστι μὲν γὰρ ὁμολογουμένως ζῶν τε καὶ ἐνεργὴς ὁ τοῦ Πατρὸς Λόγος, καὶ πρός γε τούτῳ ζωὴ, καὶ φῶς, καὶ νοητῆς εὐωδίας ὀσμή. Οὐκοῦν ὅσοι ταῖς διὰ Μωσέως προσεδρεύουσιν ἐντολαῖς, λειτουργίαν ἔχουσι τὰ περισσὰ τῆς σκηνῆς· ἀνωφελὴς γὰρ ὁ νόμος, εἰ μὴ νοοῖτο πνευματικῶς. Ὅσοι δὲ τεθάρσηνται τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, ἅγιοί που πάντως εἰσὶν ἐν Χριστῷ, περισσὸν οὐδὲν, ἀλλ' οἱονείπως αὐτὸν ἔποχον ἔχοντες τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἄθρει δὲ, εἰ δοκεῖ, καὶ τόδε. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τὸ τί δὴ φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Οἱ μὲν γὰρ τὰ περισσὰ τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς ἐγκεχειρισμένοι φέρουσιν ἐφ' ἁμαξῶν. Κααθῖται δὲ, τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων οὐκ ἐφ' ἁμαξῶν, οὐκ ἐφ' ἑτέρου του παντελῶς, ἀλλ' ὤμοις αὐτοῖς ἐπιθέντες ᾔεσαν.
pass_a_gloss: [continuing Numbers 7 from §6:] 'and a calf/young bull from each, and they brought before the tent. And the Lord said to Moses, saying: Take from them, and they will be for the service works of the tent of witness, and you will give them to the Levites, to each according to his service. And Moses, having taken the wagons and the oxen, gave them to the Levites. And the two wagons and the four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon according to their services, and the four wagons and the eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari according to their services, through Ithamar son of Aaron the priest; and to the sons of Kohath he did not give, because they have the ministrations of the holy [place]; on shoulders they will lift.' Do you hear how for some the custom [was] to lead and carry on wagons, but for Kohathites alone, the sacred things onto shoulders? PALL.: For the sake of what? CYR.: For always somehow in greater sweat is what excels and is more sacred, and there follows it in every way and entirely: the needing to labour, and besides this the enduring of suffering, and not in equal [measure] with the others, [for] those who would be holier and nearer as it were to God. Or is what I say not true? PALL.: Certainly. CYR.: In such order then the Levitical race served. But I think the matter fills a type of a mystery. PALL.: How do you say? CYR.: For the two clans, Gershon and Merari, seem to hint at the peoples in the law, I mean Israel; and the Kohathites, those sanctified in Christ through faith. For to the ones were in care the hangings of the court, the hide curtains of the tent, the coverings and the pillars, heads and bases, pegs and hangings around, and, as the sacred Writing says, 'all the extra things', through which is signified what is not necessary of the service. And the others were trusted (pass.) to carry the holy of holies, and the things through which Christ is signified not in one manner but rather in many ways and many forms: as ark, as table, and as golden lampstand, and golden incense altar. For being simple by nature as God, by the difference/variety of his working he is made known in many ways. For confessedly the Word of the Father is living and active, and besides this life and light, and odour of intelligible/spiritual fragrance. Therefore as many as attend on the commandments through Moses have as service the extra things of the tent; for the law is useless unless understood spiritually. But as many as have been trusted with the holy of holies are surely holy in Christ, [having] nothing extra, but as it were having Emmanuel himself riding/seated upon them. PALL.: You spoke well. CYR.: Look, if it seems good, at this too. PALL.: What do you say? CYR.: For those entrusted with the extra things of the holy tent carry on wagons. But Kohathites, the holy of holies not on wagons, not on anything else whatever, but having set [them] on the shoulders themselves, went.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …and a young bull from each, and they brought them before the tent. And the Lord said to Moses: Take these from them, and they shall be used for the works of service of the tent of witness, and you shall give them to the Levites, to each according to his service. So Moses took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites. Two wagons and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to their services, and four wagons and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their services, under Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because they have the services of the holy place: they shall carry them on their shoulders.’ (Numbers 7:3–9) Do you hear how the others were accustomed to move and carry things on wagons, but the Kohathites alone carried the holy things on their shoulders?

Cyril: Because what ranks higher and is more sacred always calls, in some way, for greater sweat. In every way and without fail it brings with it, for those who are holier and, as it were, nearer to God, the need to toil and, beyond that, to endure hardship, and not in the same measure as the others. Or is what I say not true?
Cyril: In this order, then, the Levitical tribe performed its service. But I for my part think the arrangement fulfills the type of a mystery.

Cyril: The two clans, Gershon and Merari, seem to hint at the peoples under the law, I mean Israel, and the Kohathites at those sanctified in Christ through faith. The former had in their care the hangings of the court, the hide curtains of the tent, the coverings and the pillars, the capitals and the bases, the pegs and the screens, and, as Holy Scripture says, ‘all the extra things’ (Numbers 4:26), by which is meant what is not essential in the service. The Kohathites were entrusted with carrying the most holy things, the things through which Christ is signified, not in a single way, but rather in many ways and many forms: as the ark, as the table, as the golden lampstand, and as the golden altar of incense. For though he is simple by nature, as God, he is made known in many ways through the variety of his works. For the Word of the Father is, as all confess, living and active (Hebrews 4:12), and besides this he is life and light (John 1:4), and the scent of a spiritual fragrance. So those who devote themselves to the commandments given through Moses have the extra things of the tent as their service, for the law is of no use unless it is understood spiritually. But those entrusted with the most holy things are surely holy in Christ. They carry nothing extra, but bear, as it were, Emmanuel himself seated upon them.
Cyril: Consider this as well, if you will.

Cyril: Those entrusted with the extra things of the holy tent carry them on wagons. But the Kohathites carried the most holy things not on wagons, and not on anything else at all; they set them on their own shoulders and so went on their way.

choices.why: μόσχος rendered 'young bull' (LXX Numbers 7:3 has μόσχον where the list says 'oxen').
διὰ Ἰθάμαρ rendered 'under Ithamar' (by the hand of, Numbers 7:8).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 13 to compare. Sense taken from the PG 68 Greek. The withheld earlier English was not used as a model.

apparatus.note: PG 68.856. Opens inside the quotation of Numbers 7:2-9 begun at the end of §6; the English begins with an ellipsis. μόσχος rendered 'young bull' (LXX Numbers 7:3 has μόσχον where the list says 'oxen'). διὰ Ἰθάμαρ rendered 'under Ithamar' (by the hand of, Numbers 7:8). 'All the extra things' (πάντα τὰ περισσά) is Cyril's citation of the LXX wording for the Gershonites' load (Numbers 4:26, 'καὶ τὰ περισσά'); his 'all' may be his own expansion or a reading of his text. 'Living and active' is Hebrews 4:12 (ζῶν ... καὶ ἐνεργής), here applied to the Word as Person; 'life and light' follows John 1:4. 'The scent of a spiritual fragrance' may recall 2 Corinthians 2:14-15, but the wording differs; no citation. 'In many ways and many forms' (πολλαχῶς ... καὶ πολυειδῶς) resembles Hebrews 1:1 (πολυμερῶς καὶ πολυτρόπως) but is not a quotation; no citation. 'Sanctified in Christ through faith' resembles 1 Corinthians 1:2 and Acts 26:18 but is a common phrase; no citation. 'The law is of no use' (ἀνωφελὴς ὁ νόμος) may echo Hebrews 7:18 (τὸ ... ἀνωφελές), but Cyril limits it ('unless it is understood spiritually'), so it is left uncited; the old English printed Galatians 3:24 and Hebrews 7:18 after the last sentence of this section, where neither verse is quoted. Emmanuel is the title from Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23, used as a name; no citation. ἐθαρσήθησαν / τεθάρσηνται taken as passive 'were entrusted with' (θαρρέω, to be trusted with). ἔποχος ('mounted on, riding on') rendered 'seated upon them', the image of a rider carried by his bearers.
